subject.title: [Feature]: Support arbitrary workspace files in bootstrap context injection

question: Should OpenClaw accept explicitly configured custom-basename workspace files in the bundled bootstrap-extra-files hook contract?
rationale: The source change is mechanically clear, but it changes system-prompt context loading scope and config-visible behavior, which repository policy treats as a product/security boundary decision.

options.title: Approve guarded custom files
options.body: Allow explicitly configured custom-basename files through the existing hook after the implementation preserves containment, budgets, diagnostics, session filtering, and docs.

options.title: Keep recognized basenames only
options.body: Reject arbitrary workspace-file injection and keep this hook limited to first-class bootstrap filenames until a broader context model is approved.

options.title: Defer to a convention/API design
options.body: Use the linked capabilities/context-discovery discussions to design a broader workspace context convention before changing runtime loading.

recommendation.title: Approve guarded custom files
recommendation.body: Allow explicitly configured custom-basename files through the existing hook after the implementation preserves containment, budgets, diagnostics, session filtering, and docs.

likelyOwner.reason: He merged the original bootstrap hook feature and is the best available owner for the core context-loading product decision.
